questions.stem: Ms Thomas, 56, has bilateral hip, knee and hand pain that is worse on weight-bearing, with morning stiffness under 30 minutes. You move to examine her hips with her lying supine on the GP couch. Which manoeuvre is most sensitive for early hip osteoarthritis?
options: Thomas test with the opposite hip held fully flexed, checking the resting thigh position
Trendelenburg test standing on each leg in turn
Passive internal rotation with the hip and knee flexed to 90 degrees
Straight leg raise to 70 degrees with ankle dorsiflexion
questions.why: Internal rotation is the first movement lost in hip osteoarthritis. Testing it passively with the hip and knee flexed to 90 degrees often reproduces groin pain and shows reduced range early, before other signs appear.
notes: A fixed flexion deformity is a late sign of advanced hip disease, so it misses early osteoarthritis.
The Trendelenburg test assesses hip abductor (gluteus medius) function and is not a sensitive test for early joint disease.
The straight leg raise tests for lumbosacral nerve root tension in radicular pain, and she has no leg symptoms.

questions.stem: Ms Thomas, 56, has nodal hand osteoarthritis and knee osteoarthritis. CRP, ESR, RF and anti-CCP are normal, eGFR is over 90, and she has no GI, kidney or cardiac history. She has started exercise and is working on weight loss, and she asks for something for the knee and hand pain. Which medicine is the most appropriate first choice?
options: Paracetamol 1 g orally four times daily, taken regularly for at least 4 weeks as a trial
Topical diclofenac gel to the painful knees and hands, 3 to 4 times daily
Tramadol 50 mg orally up to four times daily as needed
Glucosamine sulfate 1500 mg orally once daily
questions.why: For knee and hand osteoarthritis, a topical NSAID is the first-line medicine. It relieves pain about as well as an oral NSAID, with far less systemic GI, kidney and cardiovascular risk. Use it alongside exercise and weight loss.
notes: Paracetamol gives at most a small, clinically trivial benefit in osteoarthritis and is no longer preferred first-line.
Opioids, including tramadol, are not recommended for osteoarthritis: benefit is small and the risk of harm and dependence is significant.
Glucosamine is not recommended because good-quality trials show no meaningful benefit over placebo.

questions.stem: Ms Thomas, 56, has bony Heberden's and Bouchard's nodes. Her hand X-ray shows joint space narrowing, marginal osteophytes and subchondral sclerosis, with no erosions or periarticular osteopenia, and her CRP is 4 mg/L. Which underlying process best explains these findings?
options: Autoimmune synovitis with pannus formation, eroding bone at the joint margins over time
Urate crystal deposition provoking neutrophil-driven inflammation
Enthesitis at tendon insertions with new bone formation
Cartilage loss under mechanical load, with reactive bone remodelling
questions.why: Osteoarthritis is a whole-joint disease. Articular cartilage breaks down, and the subchondral bone remodels in response, forming osteophytes (the nodes) and sclerosis. Because the inflammation is only low grade, CRP stays normal and there are no erosions.
notes: Rheumatoid pannus causes marginal erosions, periarticular osteopenia and raised inflammatory markers, and none of these are present.
Gout causes acute hot swollen joints and punched-out erosions with overhanging edges, which she has never had.
Enthesitis with new bone formation is typical of spondyloarthritis such as psoriatic arthritis, and she has no psoriasis, nail changes or erosive change.

questions.stem: Examining the hands of Ms Thomas, 56, you note squaring at the base of each thumb, caused by adduction and subluxation of the base of the first metacarpal, and pain on grinding the thumb base. She can no longer open jars. Which joint is affected, and which bones form it?
options: First carpometacarpal joint: trapezium with the base of the first metacarpal
First metacarpophalangeal joint: first metacarpal head with proximal phalanx
Scaphotrapeziotrapezoid joint: scaphoid with the trapezium and trapezoid
Radiocarpal joint: distal radius with the scaphoid and the lunate
questions.why: Thumb-base squaring and a positive grind test point to the first carpometacarpal (trapeziometacarpal) joint. It is a saddle joint between the trapezium and the base of the first metacarpal, and one of the most common sites of hand osteoarthritis.
notes: The first MCP joint lies further along the thumb and does not cause squaring at the base of the thumb.
The STT joint is often involved alongside the CMC joint, but it lies deeper in the carpus and does not produce the squared thumb base.
The radiocarpal (wrist) joint is not typically involved in nodal osteoarthritis and would not cause thumb-base squaring.
